thread:
marta-sales: heads-up — Orion Bank POC asked for: 1) a simple residency diagram showing where data flows for Hosted / Dedicated / Private, 2) proof we can use customer-owned keys (they call it per-tenant CMK), and 3) an evidence pack for any human access to customer data. want a short deliverable set by EOD tomorrow. can we do?

leo-se: quick summary: Private = full customer KMS/HSM control. Dedicated = BYOK supported (we store wrapped keys only). Hosted = Redwood KMS today; we can negotiate envelope-key patterns but NOT per-tenant CMK on hosted.

nina-arch: rough ASCII sketch i'll refine into SVG after we lock language:
```
Client -> Ingress (Regional) -> Router -> Model Pool (gpu-nodes)
                       |-> KV cache (tenant-scoped, encrypted)
                       |-> Key service: Redwood KMS or Customer KMS (BYOK for Dedicated/Private)
Audit -> Immutable store -> Signed export -> Customer SIEM/S3
```

sam-security: retention & meta notes: we default to not storing full plaintext. stored metadata: request_id, model_id, duration_ms, token_counts, timestamp, tenant_id, route. debug snapshots are redacted by default and require security approval. access events (human/operator) include actor, justification, timestamp and are signed.

marta-sales: they also pressed on cache leakage risk between tenants — short, plain answer?

sam-security: runtime caches are namespaced per-tenant, include ACL checks, and are encrypted at rest. on scale-down or model reload we zero cache segments. any cross-tenant access would be a security incident and triggers full forensics; we can include that wording.

leo-se: for the one-pager i'll include: KMS modes, cache isolation, what metadata we persist, evidence SLA for access logs, and subprocessor disclosure cadence. also add a short paragraph on how we handle field-level encryption/tokenization for hosted endpoints if they need higher isolation.

oliver-legal: they want a 3rd-party subprocessor attestation and a promise to provide on-demand signed evidence within 72 hours. legal is comfortable offering 72h for enterprise contracts (scoped). add: monthly subprocessor list and emergency notification for material changes.

marta-sales: good. can ops produce a sample signed-access bundle format to include? customer expects to verify signatures.

ops-bot: POC-ORION-502 created and assigned to leo-se  https://redwood.internal/pocs/POC-ORION-502

sam-security: sample bundle example we can hand them (strip down): {"events":[{"actor":"ops-user","action":"ssh-run","target":"gpu-012","time":"2025-06-01T12:00:00Z","justification":"debug"}],"signature":"MEUCIQD..."} plus verification steps using our pubkey. i'll attach verification commands in the artifact.

nina-arch: cc @sam-security i'll export the diagram as SVG and include the legend about what is and isn't persisted. also include a short note: Private deployments have no Redwood subprocessors by default; Dedicated uses limited subprocessors (listed), Hosted uses our standard subproc list.

leo-se: timeline: draft one-pager + diagram + subproc list + example signed bundle by tomorrow 3pm PT. i'll drop into the POC ticket.

oliver-legal: i'll review the wording on the subproc commitment after draft. we should avoid promising SLA for hosted without enterprise amendment.

marta-sales: thanks team. Orion wants the packet asap to unblock procurement. i'll follow up with their security lead once artifacts are uploaded. :rocket:
